items.stem:
Read the passage below and answer the questions that follow.

Together We Grow

1. A co-operative is a group of people who join together to meet a common need. Members own it, run it and share its benefits. The idea is simple: what one small farmer, weaver or fisher cannot do alone, many can do together.

2. Take a group of women in a village who make pickles at home. Alone, each sells a few jars to neighbours. Together, they can buy spices in bulk at a lower price, share a kitchen, design a common label and send their products to shops in the city. Their income rises, and so does their confidence.

3. Co-operatives work best when members trust one another. Decisions are taken democratically – usually one member, one vote – and accounts are kept open so that everyone can see where the money goes. When trust breaks down, a co-operative can fail.

4. India has thousands of co-operatives today, in dairy, sugar, banking, housing and handicrafts. The most famous began with milk in Gujarat and grew into a brand known across the country. Its success showed that ordinary people, working together honestly, can build something extraordinary.

(i) What is a co-operative?
(ii) Who owns a co-operative?  (a) Nobody  (b) A single rich trader  (c) A foreign company  (d) Its members
(iii) How do the pickle makers benefit from working together?
(iv) What does "in bulk" mean?  (a) on credit  (b) secretly  (c) in small packets  (d) in large quantities
(v) On what does the success of a co-operative depend most?  (a) Luck  (b) Trust among members  (c) The weather  (d) Advertising
(vi) How are decisions usually taken in a co-operative?  (a) By a foreign manager  (b) Democratically – one member, one vote  (c) By the oldest member alone  (d) By a lottery
(vii) Why are accounts kept open?
(viii) Name two fields in which India has co-operatives.
(ix) Which famous co-operative is referred to in the last paragraph?  (a) A sugar mill in Bihar  (b) A bank in Kerala  (c) A housing society in Delhi  (d) The milk co-operative of Gujarat that became Amul
(x) Which word in paragraph 4 means "very unusual or remarkable"?  (a) extraordinary  (b) ordinary  (c) famous  (d) honestly
items.answer: (i) A group of people who join together to meet a common need, owning and running it and sharing benefits. (ii) (d) Its members (iii) They buy spices cheaply in bulk, share a kitchen, use a common label and sell in the city; income and confidence rise. (iv) (d) in large quantities (v) (b) Trust among members (vi) (b) Democratically – one member, one vote (vii) So that every member can see where the money goes, which builds trust. (viii) Dairy, sugar, banking, housing, handicrafts (any two). (ix) (d) The milk co-operative of Gujarat that became Amul (x) (a) extraordinary
items.markingKey: (i) A group of people who join together to meet a common need, owning and running it and sharing benefits. (ii) (d) Its members (iii) They buy spices cheaply in bulk, share a kitchen, use a common label and sell in the city; income and confidence rise. (iv) (d) in large quantities (v) (b) Trust among members (vi) (b) Democratically – one member, one vote (vii) So that every member can see where the money goes, which builds trust. (viii) Dairy, sugar, banking, housing, handicrafts (any two). (ix) (d) The milk co-operative of Gujarat that became Amul (x) (a) extraordinary (1 mark each, 10 marks.)

items.stem:
Read the survey report and answer the questions that follow.

A survey on care for elderly neighbours was carried out in Nagpur in 2025. 500 residents of a housing society were asked how often they spend time with elderly people in their area. The results were: daily – 12%; every week – 19%; once a month – 16%; hardly ever – 53%. The word "companionship" came up often in the discussion that followed the survey.

(i) Which response was the most common?  (a) hardly ever  (b) once a month  (c) every week  (d) daily
(ii) Which response was the least common?  (a) once a month  (b) daily  (c) every week  (d) hardly ever
(iii) How many residents of a housing society chose "daily"?  (a) 600  (b) 60  (c) 95  (d) 12
(iv) By how many percentage points does "daily" differ from "every week"?  (a) 4  (b) 7  (c) 12  (d) 31
(v) What percentage of residents of a housing society chose one of the two most common responses taken together?  (a) 53%  (b) 82%  (c) 72%  (d) 28%
(vi) Did more than half of the residents of a housing society choose "hardly ever"? Give the figure.
(vii) Which of these statements is supported by the survey?  (a) "hardly ever" was chosen by more residents of a housing society than "every week".  (b) "daily" was chosen by more residents of a housing society than "hardly ever".  (c) The survey was carried out in Mysuru.  (d) Every response was chosen by the same number of residents of a housing society.
(viii) Suggest one reason why "daily" may have been chosen by so few residents of a housing society.
(ix) What fraction of the residents of a housing society did NOT choose "daily"? Answer as a percentage.  (a) 81%  (b) 88%  (c) 12%  (d) 38%
(x) Rank the top three responses, starting with the most common.
items.answer: (i) (a) hardly ever (ii) (b) daily (iii) (b) 60 (iv) (b) 7 (v) (c) 72% (vi) Yes – 53%, which is more than half. (vii) (a) "hardly ever" was chosen by more residents of a housing society than "every week". (viii) Any sensible reason linked to the context (cost, habit, lack of access, awareness, time) – 1 mark. (ix) (b) 88% (x) hardly ever, every week, once a month

items.stem:
Read the passage below, based on the play 'Wisdom Paves the Way', and answer.

"The court fell silent as the eldest brother finished his account. 'We never saw the animal, Your Majesty,' he said. 'We only read the road as a scholar reads a book.' The king leaned forward, a slow smile spreading across his face. 'Then you have taught my whole court a lesson today,' he said."

Answer the following:
(i) What did the eldest brother claim?
(ii) "We only read the road as a scholar reads a book" is an example of …  (a) alliteration  (b) a simile  (c) onomatopoeia  (d) a pun
(iii) How did the king react?
(iv) What lesson might the court have learnt?
(v) Which word shows that the king was interested?  (a) finished  (b) court  (c) silent  (d) leaned
items.answer: (i) That they had never seen the animal and had only read the clues on the road. (ii) (b) a simile (iii) He smiled and said the brothers had taught his court a lesson. (iv) That careful observation and honest reasoning can reveal the truth. (v) (d) leaned
items.markingKey: (i) That they had never seen the animal and had only read the clues on the road. (ii) (b) a simile (iii) He smiled and said the brothers had taught his court a lesson. (iv) That careful observation and honest reasoning can reveal the truth. (v) (d) leaned (1 mark each, 5 marks.)

Read the passage below, based on the poem 'Harvest Hymn', and answer.

"When the last sheaf of rice was tied, old Kaveri-amma set down her sickle and looked up at the sky. 'You gave us rain when we begged for it,' she said softly, 'and sun when the grain needed it. What can we give you in return?' The children laughed, but she was not joking. She left the first handful of grain at the edge of the field."

Answer the following:
(i) What had just been finished?
(ii) Whom is Kaveri-amma speaking to?  (a) The sky/nature  (b) The children  (c) Her sickle  (d) A shopkeeper
(iii) Which poetic device is used when she speaks to the sky?  (a) simile  (b) apostrophe  (c) pun  (d) alliteration
(iv) Why did she leave the first handful of grain at the edge of the field?
(v) What does this passage share with the poem "Harvest Hymn"?
items.answer: (i) Tying the last sheaf of rice – the harvest. (ii) (a) The sky/nature (iii) (b) apostrophe (iv) As an offering of thanks to nature for the harvest. (v) Both express gratitude to nature for the harvest.
items.markingKey: (i) Tying the last sheaf of rice – the harvest. (ii) (a) The sky/nature (iii) (b) apostrophe (iv) As an offering of thanks to nature for the harvest. (v) Both express gratitude to nature for the harvest. (1 mark each, 5 marks.)

items.stem:
Read the passage below and answer the questions that follow.

Together We Grow

1. A co-operative is a group of people who join together to meet a common need. Members own it, run it and share its benefits. The idea is simple: what one small farmer, weaver or fisher cannot do alone, many can do together.

2. Take a group of women in a village who make pickles at home. Alone, each sells a few jars to neighbours. Together, they can buy spices in bulk at a lower price, share a kitchen, design a common label and send their products to shops in the city. Their income rises, and so does their confidence.

3. Co-operatives work best when members trust one another. Decisions are taken democratically – usually one member, one vote – and accounts are kept open so that everyone can see where the money goes. When trust breaks down, a co-operative can fail.

4. India has thousands of co-operatives today, in dairy, sugar, banking, housing and handicrafts. The most famous began with milk in Gujarat and grew into a brand known across the country. Its success showed that ordinary people, working together honestly, can build something extraordinary.

(i) What is a co-operative?
(ii) Who owns a co-operative?  (a) A foreign company  (b) Nobody  (c) Its members  (d) A single rich trader
(iii) How do the pickle makers benefit from working together?
(iv) Which word in paragraph 2 shows that the women became more self-assured?  (a) neighbours  (b) income  (c) confidence  (d) label
(v) On what does the success of a co-operative depend most?  (a) Luck  (b) The weather  (c) Advertising  (d) Trust among members
(vi) How are decisions usually taken in a co-operative?  (a) By the oldest member alone  (b) By a foreign manager  (c) Democratically – one member, one vote  (d) By a lottery
(vii) Why are accounts kept open?
(viii) Name two fields in which India has co-operatives.
(ix) Which famous co-operative is referred to in the last paragraph?  (a) A bank in Kerala  (b) A sugar mill in Bihar  (c) The milk co-operative of Gujarat that became Amul  (d) A housing society in Delhi
(x) Which word in paragraph 4 means "very unusual or remarkable"?  (a) famous  (b) extraordinary  (c) ordinary  (d) honestly
items.answer: (i) A group of people who join together to meet a common need, owning and running it and sharing benefits. (ii) (c) Its members (iii) They buy spices cheaply in bulk, share a kitchen, use a common label and sell in the city; income and confidence rise. (iv) (c) confidence (v) (d) Trust among members (vi) (c) Democratically – one member, one vote (vii) So that every member can see where the money goes, which builds trust. (viii) Dairy, sugar, banking, housing, handicrafts (any two). (ix) (c) The milk co-operative of Gujarat that became Amul (x) (b) extraordinary

Read the survey report and answer the questions that follow.

A survey on music in daily life was carried out in Jaipur in 2025. 400 students were asked when they listen to music most. The results were: while studying – 32%; while travelling – 20%; while exercising – 17%; before sleeping – 13%; rarely or never – 18%. The word "soothing" came up often in the discussion that followed the survey.

(i) Which response was the most common?  (a) while travelling  (b) while studying  (c) while exercising  (d) rarely or never
(ii) Which response was the least common?  (a) rarely or never  (b) while travelling  (c) while studying  (d) before sleeping
(iii) How many students chose "before sleeping"?  (a) 13  (b) 520  (c) 52  (d) 68
(iv) By how many percentage points does "before sleeping" differ from "while exercising"?  (a) 4  (b) 9  (c) 30  (d) 1
(v) What percentage of students chose one of the two most common responses taken together?  (a) 48%  (b) 32%  (c) 62%  (d) 52%
(vi) Did more than half of the students choose "while studying"? Give the figure.
(vii) Which of these statements is supported by the survey?  (a) The survey was carried out in Dehradun.  (b) "while studying" was chosen by more students than "while travelling".  (c) "before sleeping" was chosen by more students than "while studying".  (d) Every response was chosen by the same number of students.
(viii) Suggest one reason why "before sleeping" may have been chosen by so few students.
(ix) Write one suggestion the organisers could make, based on the survey on music in daily life.
(x) What fraction of the students did NOT choose "before sleeping"? Answer as a percentage.  (a) 37%  (b) 13%  (c) 87%  (d) 83%
items.answer: (i) (b) while studying (ii) (d) before sleeping (iii) (c) 52 (iv) (a) 4 (v) (d) 52% (vi) No – 32%, which is less than half. (vii) (b) "while studying" was chosen by more students than "while travelling". (viii) Any sensible reason linked to the context (cost, habit, lack of access, awareness, time) – 1 mark. (ix) Any practical suggestion that follows from the figures – 1 mark. (x) (c) 87%
items.markingKey: (i) (b) while studying (ii) (d) before sleeping (iii) (c) 52 (iv) (a) 4 (v) (d) 52% (vi) No – 32%, which is less than half. (vii) (b) "while studying" was chosen by more students than "while travelling". (viii) Any sensible reason linked to the context (cost, habit, lack of access, awareness, time) – 1 mark.
